key_idea: Construct a fractal branching block to produce a potential carrying opposite limiting charges, which then defines a scalar multiplier that transforms the conductivity while exactly preserving the boundary measurements.
reason: The proof rests on a highly unexpected and conceptually beautiful insight—using a fractal structure to generate a scalar change of variables that fools the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. However, realizing this idea requires a dense and intricate apparatus involving convex integration, laminates, Baire category arguments, and precise geometric matching.
recognized: Counterexample to the Calderón problem for bounded conductivities in dimensions n>=3 (recent breakthrough)
